2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptor filed a case for pre-emption of the case land under section .96 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Baliakhandi being Misc. Case No. 20 of 1992, alleging inter alia that he is a co-sharer in the case jote by inheritance as well as by purchase while the pre-emplee is a stranger thereto. By the impugned kabala dated 11.4.92 opposite party No. 2 sold the case land measuring 2.10 acres to the pre-emptee opposite party No. 1 at a consideration of Tk. 55000/- only by registered kabala dated 11.4.92 without serving the statutory notice upon him. Subsequently, after learning about the disputed kabala he obtained the certified copy of the same and thereafter filed the pre-emption case on making the statutory deposit impleding necessary parties. It was also alleged that he is a bonafide cultivator and he is enti-tled to pre-emption. 3. The pre-emptee petitioner contested the case by filing written objection denying all the material allegations of the pre-emption application and contended inter alia that the case is bad for defect of parties and it is barred by the principles of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel. It was also contended that after the purchase of the case land he made improvements in it by spending a huge amount of money, and if pre-emption is allowed, he is entitled to improvement cost. 

 7. Mr. Chandi Charan Paul, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in view of the fact that the two sons of the admitted co-sharer Nitya Gopal Biswas have subsisting interest at least to the extent of decimal of land in the case jote but they have not being impleaded in the case, and as such the case is clearly bad for defect of parties and consequently the learned court of appeal below clearly erred in law in allowing pre-emption, in relation of the mandatory provision of section 91(1) of the Slate Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950 and on this ground along the impugned judgment is liable to be set in the interest of justice. Mr. Pal further submits that the learned Courts below also erred in law in not allowing improvement cost to the petition-er arbitrarily and the same has accessioned failure of justice. 

 12. It has been clearly stated in the  pre-emption application that Nitya Gopal 4, Biswas sold 71 decimals by of land to Makhanlal Biswas by registered kabala dated 13.6.75 and thereafter he sold topetitioners father Haripada Biswas 14 decimals by registered kabala dated 27.5.74, marked Ext. 3 (ka) and 3 (Kha) respectively and with these sales he became completely divested of all interests in the suit jote. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that even after the aforesaid two sales, Natiya Copal Biswas was left with decimals of land in the case jote and as such he continued to be a co-sharer in the case jote and as such he was a necessary party to the pre-emption case and after him his two sons have become, co-sharers in the case jote and as such for nor impleading them in the case the pre-emption case must be held to be bad for defect of parties. 

 16. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, I am constrained to held that the cases referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioners are quite distinguishable from the facts of the present case and consequently these are no assistance to the petitioner. For the reasons stated above, I do not find any substance in this revision case.
